newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Kashmiri leader wants Blair help against India.
newsitem.headline: Kashmiri leader wants Blair help against India.

text.p: The chief executive of Pakistan-ruled Kashmir on Friday greeted new British Prime Minister Tony Blair and urged him to pressure India to settle the Kashmir dispute.

"The prospects of the resolution of the long-standing issue of Kashmir have also become bright with the coming in of your party in power," Azad (free) Kashmir Prime Minister Sultan Mahmood Chaudhry said in a message sent to Blair, according to a state government statement.
It quoted Chaudhry as saying that Kashmiris, many of whom live in Britain, expected the Labour government to "exert due pressure" on India to resolve the Kashmir dispute with Pakistan.
Blair was quoted by India's Hindustan Times as saying his government would seek to help negotiate an agreement on Kashmir between India and Pakistan.
India rules two-thirds and Pakistan the rest of Kashmir, over which the two countries have fought two of their three wars since their independence from Britain in 1947.
India is fighting a Moslem separatist revolt in its part of Kashmir since 1990.
Chaudhry visited Britain during the election campaign, urging Kashmiris living there in speeches to vote for the party that supported their case against India.
